Share SOC2/ISO docs and VPC deployment checklist

Ethan Zhao: Prepare benchmark run plan + request sample traffic by 2025-05-23

summary: Redwood AE and SE ran a focused demo on rate limiting, quotas, and org/project API key controls for Metris Health. Covered how org-level quotas and per-project keys work in the Console and API, enforcement behaviors (429 vs queuing), and how Optimize recommendations (batching/caching) reduce per-token cost under multi-tenant loads. Security topics (KMS, audit logs, SSO, RBAC) and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private) were discussed. Agreed next steps: share pricing spreadsheet, SOC2 docs, and schedule a POC benchmark next week.
topics: Rate limiting model-level and org-level quotas
Project & org API keys and scoping
Dedicated vs hosted routing and fallback
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-05-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhao (Redwood SE), Avery Kim (CTO - Metris), Jordan Lee (Platform/Infra - Metris), Priya Nair (Security/SRE - Metris)

[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Avery (Metris): yep, loud and clear. thanks Samira.
[00:12] Samira: awesome. quick agenda — we'll show the Console flow for org and project keys, demo rate limits and quotas, a quick walkthrough of Optimize suggestions for cost, and then leave time for security questions. Ethan will drive the technical bits.
[00:28] Ethan (Redwood SE): hi, hi. i'll share my screen — okay sharing. you should see the Redwood Console, org settings.
[00:36] Jordan (Metris): seeing it. can you make the font bigger? my screen is small.
[00:40] Ethan: sure. so first up, org keys — we have two primitives: org-level API keys which carry org quotas and project-scoped keys for tenant isolation. for your multi-tenant platform you can create per-customer project keys and restrict models or rate tiers to them.
[01:02] Priya (Metris): when you say "restrict" do you mean hard caps or soft throttling? we need deterministic failure modes for SLA pages.
[01:10] Ethan: good question. by default we enforce hard caps which return 429s once quota is exhausted. there are policies you can enable for queuing or graceful degrading to a cheaper model tier. so you pick behavior per route or per project.
[01:24] Samira: to add, we surfaced rate-limiter configs in the Console and via the API. so you can programmatically update quotas during promotions or incidents.
[01:32] Avery: what's the granularity — per-second, per-minute? we expect spiky loads during nightly batches and also steady interactive loads.
[01:40] Ethan: you can set tokens-per-minute and requests-per-second. we also support burst windows for short spikes (token burst over N seconds). internally we bucket requests by project key and optionally by model.
[01:54] Jordan: do you aggregate across projects for billing or enforce independently? we need both: isolated quotas for safety but consolidated billing.
[02:02] Samira: yep — enforcement is per-project unless you attach projects to an org-level quota. billing/charts can be aggregated at the org level in the Console.
[02:10] Priya: how are keys rotated and audited? we have strict rotation policies and need audit trails for every key usage.
[02:18] Ethan: rotation is supported via the Console with a rotate button, and we provide audit logs that include key id, project, request meta. logs are available in the Console and via S3 export or syslog to your SIEM.
[02:30] Priya: is the audit log tamper-proof? we'd prefer write-once storage or integrated with our KMS.
[02:36] Ethan: we support pushing logs to your secure storage and we also provide signed audit events in the VPC/private deployment option. for hosted customers we integrate with customer-managed KMS for key encryption at rest.
[02:49] Avery: can you show the route and fallback policy? we want requests to failover to a cheaper model when the preferred model is overloaded.
[02:58] Ethan: sure — under model routing, here's a policy: primary route to open-llama-70b, fallback route to quantized-7b. when primary latency crosses 250ms p95 or queue grows beyond X, we automatically route to fallback. you can also do percentage-based canaries.
[03:20] Jordan: does that impact token accounting? if we downgrade to a smaller model, how is cost reported?
[03:26] Samira: cost is per-model and will show in the per-route cost breakdown. Optimize gives recommendations about when downgrading yields acceptable quality loss for big savings.
[03:34] Ethan: and the billing pipeline attributes tokens to the project key used on the request, so you'll see per-project cost.
[03:41] [04:00] Samira: quick demo of creating a project key — click new project, name, attach quota profile. I'll pick a quota: 1,000,000 tokens/day, burst 200 rps, model restrictions to text-generate endpoints only.
[04:20] Samira: key created. now i'll paste a sample curl that uses the project key: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <project_key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate ...
[04:34] Jordan: if a tenant abuses the key — can we disable immediately?
[04:38] Ethan: yes, keys can be disabled instantly and you can revoke tokens; we support key rotation with zero-downtime via a two-key model.
[04:45] Priya: for compliance we need per-tenant data residency — can project keys be restricted to certain regions or VPCs?
[04:52] Ethan: for Private and Dedicated deployments, yes — you can restrict project keys to specific regions or private endpoints. for hosted, region pinning is on roadmap but current approach is routing by region and you can set org policies.
[05:08] Avery: can you show the API for programmatically updating quotas? we'd want autoscaling apps to bump quotas during known batch windows.
[05:16] Ethan: sure — /orgs/{org_id}/projects/{proj_id}/quota PATCH with JSON payload. here's a quick example — set tokens_per_minute to 20000 for a 2hr window.
[05:30] Avery: and is there a cooldown to prevent abuse from ramping quotas too fast?
[05:34] Samira: you can enforce an approval workflow; by default the API call takes immediate effect but we recommend gating via your own platform or our RBAC workflows.
[05:44] Priya: does RBAC integrate with SSO? we use Okta.
[05:49] Ethan: yes SAML/SCIM integration — you can map groups to roles (admin, billing, project-admin). Audit logs include who made quota changes.
[05:59] Jordan: on the performance side — you mentioned KV cash earlier? i think you meant KV cache. how does cache affect rate limiting?
[06:08] Ethan: yes KV cache — sorry, transcription thing — caching reduces repeated prefix computation which lowers token usage; rate limiter still counts the tokens consumed by the request. caching reduces effective token generation and thus reduces the quota burn.
[06:25] Samira: quick note on Optimize: we run offline analyses on your request distribution and suggest batching window sizes and whether prefix caching is effective for your corpus. for multi-tenant apps, Optimize can propose per-project quantization profiles.
[06:40] Avery: is quantization automatic or do you need to checkpoint models?
[06:44] Ethan: we supply quantized variants from our model catalog that are validated; you can pick them per-project. for private deployments we can assist with an on-prem quantization pipeline.
[06:55] Priya: security again — KMS integration details? we use AWS KMS with external key material.
[07:01] Ethan: supported. for private deployments you can bring your own key (BYOK) and HSM integrations; in hosted we support customer-managed KMS where keys are in your account and we encrypt artifacts with them.
[07:12] [07:30] Samira: switching to a short demo on rate-limiter behavior when quota exceeded — i'll simulate a burst.
[07:36] Ethan: hitting the endpoint with project key at high QPS... you should see 200 for first N requests then 429s once burst capacity is used.
[07:48] Jordan: yep i'm seeing 429s in the client. what's the retry-after semantics?
[07:52] Ethan: we return Retry-After header with seconds until token window resets; for token-based quotas we return an estimate of tokens available.
[07:59] Priya: do you provide client SDKs that handle retries and backoff?
[08:03] Samira: yes we provide SDKs with built-in retry/backoff strategies and vow to not retry 429s blindly — SDK surfaces the policy so you can choose rapid-fail or exponential backoff.
[08:15] Avery: for the POC we want realistic tenant mix. what's the easiest way to simulate multi-tenant traffic against a Dedicated cluster?
[08:22] Ethan: we can provide a benchmark harness — you'll get a script that simulates tenants with different token profiles. we recommend running it in your network or our se ones; for Dedicated we can run it in a staging pool.
[08:35] Jordan: how about cost simulation — can we predict cost by tenant?
[08:38] Samira: the Console cost simulator uses your traffic profiles + model selection to estimate monthly spend per-project. we'll share the spreadsheet.
[08:46] [09:00] Priya: on logging — are request-level logs PII-redacted by default? we can't have PHI in logs in our hosted account.
[09:07] Ethan: yes by default we redact user prompt inputs in hosted logs, you can opt into storing them for debug purposes in private deployments. we also support custom scrubbers.
[09:18] Priya: nice. that covers most compliance stuff. two quick questions from me: do you support per-project encryption keys, and can we rotate them independently?
[09:28] Ethan: per-project encryption with customer-managed keys is supported in Private and Dedicated; rotation can be orchestrated via the Console and we have a documented process to rewrap artifacts.
[09:38] Avery: any limitations on number of projects per org? we have thousands of tenants.
[09:43] Samira: no hard limit — but for orgs with thousands of projects we recommend Dedicated or Private and we can propose sharding schemes for routing and billing.
[09:53] Jordan: what about soft multi-tenant features like per-project caching — is caching sticky per key?
[09:58] Ethan: yes caches are keyed by project and by model+prefix hash so cross-tenant leakage is prevented.
[10:06] [10:30] Samira: we'll jump to Optimize recommendations now — Ethan, show the Optimize dashboard.
[10:34] Ethan: here's an example run: we analyzed sample traffic and suggested a batching window of 50ms and a cache TTL of 3600s for repeated prefixes which reduced token spend by ~18% in this workload. also recommended switching 12% of requests to quantized-7b.
[10:50] Avery: curious — how does Optimize validate quality loss? do you have evals integrated?
[10:55] Ethan: yes we run prompt-based evals on a holdout set — you set quality thresholds and Optimize simulates the tradeoff. it will flag regression alerts if production quality drops after a change.
[11:08] Priya: are those evals something we can run on-prem?
[11:11] Ethan: yes, for Private deployments we can run the eval harness in your environment.
[11:18] [11:30] Jordan: back to quotas — if we lift a quota temporarily for a tenant and they spike, is there a safety net to prevent cross-tenant noisy neighbor effects?
[11:38] Ethan: we have both soft and hard isolation. you can set node-level reservations (for Dedicated) and per-tenant throttles. also admission control will reject big bursts if cluster pressure is high.
[11:50] Avery: is there a support SLA for Dedicated?
[11:53] Samira: yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency targets and a support tier.
[11:58] Priya: procurement will want sample contracts and Data Processing Addendum (DPA).
[12:02] Samira: we'll include those in the security pack.
[12:06] [12:30] Ethan: showing API example for programmatic revoke — POST /keys/{key}/revoke returns 200 and you can see the key disabled in the Console.
[12:40] Jordan: good. that should be easy to integrate.
[12:46] [13:00] Samira: quick question for you — what's your timeline to decision?
[13:05] Avery: we're looking at a pilot in the next two weeks and production in Q3, assuming security checks pass and pricing is acceptable.
[13:12] Samira: great. we'll target a benchmark POC next Tue and get you the price sheet today.
[13:18] [13:45] Priya: one more: for SOC2 evidence, do you provide artifact samples or just the certificate?
[13:50] Ethan: we provide the report for review under NDA and sample artifacts for how logs and controls are implemented.
[13:58] Jordan: can we carve out a technical deep-dive for Dedicated networking with your infra folks?
[14:03] Samira: yes, we'll schedule a networking deep-dive with our infra team post-POC.
[14:10] [14:30] Ethan: back to the demo, i'll simulate a config change via API to bump a project's tokens_per_minute and show it reflected in the Console metrics; done. you can see the immediate effect in the console usage graph.
[14:48] Avery: nice.
[15:00] [15:30] Samira: wrap up — recap of action items: we'll send pricing and SOC2 docs, Ethan will prepare benchmark plan, Jordan will send traffic profiles, Priya will send security answers. any other blockers?
[15:47] Avery: none from me. thanks — this was helpful.
[16:00] Samira: great. we'll follow up over email with the artifacts (pricing link, docs: https://redwood.ai/docs/rate-limits and shared deck: https://redwood.ai/share/rate-limits-demo.pdf).
[16:18] Priya: thanks all.
[16:22] Samira: thanks, bye.
[16:25] (call ended)

Notes: Transcript contains typical ASR artifacts (mis-heard words, occasional punctuation oddities). Several references to documents and runbooks were made; links above are placeholders to the materials Samira promised to share.
